idea-plugin.name: Git Workflow Enforcer
idea-plugin.description:
Git Workflow Enforcer — Automatic Branch and Commit Validation

Stop catching Git convention violations in code reviews. Git Workflow Enforcer validates branch names, commit messages and protected branches before commits happen — keeping your Git history clean and your team consistent.

Branch Naming

  • Gitflow, trunk-based, GitHub Flow or custom regex patterns
  • Protected branches: committing directly on e.g. main is blocked or warned, per preset or .git-workflow.yaml

Commit Message Validation

  • Conventional Commits format with 11 allowed types: feat, fix, docs, style, refactor, perf, test, build, ci, chore, revert
  • Maximum subject length (default 72 characters)
  • Optional JIRA/issue key requirement

IDE Integration

  • Status bar widget with the current branch's compliance status
  • Pre-commit check with Commit Anyway / Cancel
  • Violations tool window grouped by type, with fix suggestions

Team Configuration

  • Shared .git-workflow.yaml versioned in Git, read on every check
  • Workflow presets: Gitflow, Trunk-Based, GitHub Flow, Custom

Requirements

  • IntelliJ IDEA 2023.2+ (or another IntelliJ-based IDE, build 232+)
  • Git4Idea plugin (bundled with all JetBrains IDEs)

Support

  • GitHub: github.com/JirakJ/git-workflow-enforcer
  • Issues: Report a Bug
  • Author: Jakub Jirák
idea-plugin.change-notes:
2026.9.1

  • Added: the pre-commit check flags committing directly on a protected branch (from the preset or the merge: section of .git-workflow.yaml: block_direct_push = error, require_pr alone = warning).
  • Fixed: branch-name validation in the pre-commit check no longer depends on the commit-message toggle.
  • Removed: the never-called base-branch and merge-direction checks; allowed_base is accepted but ignored.

2026.9.0

  • Removed: Settings that had no effect: "merge policy validation", "Conventional Commits", "require issue reference", "max subject length" and "protected branches". These rules always came from the selected preset or .git-workflow.yaml; the settings page now says so.
  • Removed: Documentation of features that do not exist: merge/push policy enforcement, merge direction checks, required reviewers, pre-push hook, config auto-reload, audit log and the compliance dashboard.
  • Fixed: The README .git-workflow.yaml example used keys the loader does not read (branchRules, allowedBase, commitRules, …); it now uses the real keys (branches, allowed_base, commits, max_subject_length, …).
  • Fixed: An unknown preset name stored in settings no longer breaks the settings page.

2026.8.0

  • The plugin is now completely free — all features unlocked, no license needed.
  • Source code is now open source under Apache-2.0: https://github.com/JirakJ/git-workflow-enforcer
